THE TWO DRUG PRICE ELASTICITIES, measured 30 August.

WHICH POINT THIS IS. The run tag is 3fdcabf7ae, NOT d6ed8b6e2a. Those are the
same economics under two names: d6ed8b6e2a is the md5 of the 26-name vector as
it stood before kappa_phi_d_level entered it, and 3fdcabf7ae is the md5 of the
same 26 values plus kappa_phi_d_level=8.0, which is the level d6ed8b6e2a
already solved at (it was settable in the Fortran and not handable, so every
point before 30 August solved at its declared 8.0). run_one_point.sh computes
both and calls the shorter one LEGACY_TAG; points/point_d6ed8b6e2a.txt had to
be moved out of the way for this run, because the legacy-skip branch would
otherwise have exited without solving. It has since been restored untouched.
The log this block was copied from is code/worker_3fdcabf7ae.log. The vector is
line 1 of code/MORTALITY.txt with kappa_phi_d_level moved from 2.0 to 8.0, and
the run reported HANDOVER OK: 26 of 26 parameters applied, 51 min on 4 cores.

WHAT WAS DIFFERENT ABOUT THE BINARY. measure_price_elasticity was flipped from
0 to 1 in the checkout for this run only, and was NOT committed. The point file
this run wrote, points/point_3fdcabf7ae.txt, is deliberately NOT committed
either: it reproduces an existing point's economics on a changed binary and
must not enter the archive.

WHICH SOURCE IT SOLVED ON, AND WHY THAT IS STILL THE RIGHT NUMBER. The solve
ran on cedf712, and origin has since moved to 190e54a, which corrects the
model: three accumulators for users -- model_avg_income_drug_users,
model_average_assets_drug_users and model_average_income_addicted -- were
summed over households that BUY drugs while being divided by a mass that counts
every household CARRYING the disorder. That correction does not reach these
elasticities. Both are log ratios of model_total_drug_users and
model_drugs_used_by_users_on_average across the price step, neither of those
two is touched by the diff, and all four changed sites are statistics
accumulators downstream of the distribution with no feedback into policy or
prices. The income statistics in the block below ARE the pre-correction ones
and should be read from a point solved on 190e54a instead.

THE RESULT. Both elasticities were measured; neither hit a HELD branch. This is
the first time the block has run to completion.

  participation   model = -1.0275218181739272   observed = -0.63
  intensive       model = -5.0587723352865224   observed = -0.55

  base   price = 1.0000000000000000  users = 8.6726249786061457E-002
         quantity per user = 4.1448502087735338E-002
  +10%   price = 1.1000000014901161  users = 7.8635504844853765E-002
         quantity per user = 2.5592497327820315E-002

Both are the right sign and both overshoot; the intensive margin overshoots by
roughly a factor of nine. Note that the moments block below CONTAINS the whole
second solve, because the elasticity block runs between the ALL TARGETED
MOMENTS and END OF MOMENTS markers -- the age loop and distribution output
from line ~165 of the block onward is that second solve at the higher price,
not the benchmark.

ONE EDIT TO THE COPIED BLOCK. A single line of 8 NUL bytes appeared in the
second solve's convergence output (between the DIST_MOM line and
"distribution distance="). The NUL bytes are stripped here so this file is
plain text and diffable; nothing else is altered.
